analysis.title: GS Basics: AI Firmly Bid. French Concerns. Rate Vol (Rich Privorotsky, FICC & Equities, 1 Oct 2026)
key_insights: Asia opened firmly bid after Micron's results, led by semiconductors. Nikkei was up as much as 3%, KOSPI +1.7% and Taiwan +0.8%. The desk attributes part of the move to a rapid reversion of month-end and quarter-end softness in the US close the day before.

AI view is unchanged and the desk calls it the clearest investable theme. Cited support: accelerating inference demand, new product launches (Muse, Dots, Autopilot, Grok bots), Google's Gemini 4/Argon release overnight (strong benchmarks, limited real-world evidence), and Oracle's reported ~$7bn Tencent deal for ~100k advanced chips.

Compute is physically scarce. H200/B200 rental pricing remains extremely firm and spot compute is scarce. Polymarket prices 20-30% odds of state-level data center moratoriums by end 2027. The desk argues that if compute keeps gaining value because supply is short, it is hard to be bearish the suppliers of compute (optical, power behind the meter, utilization, stranded capacity).

Micron: the desk argues pricing is rising faster than expected, FY27 supply/demand remains tight, Q1 margins are the floor, and 2027 HBM pricing is materially above 2026. After the multiple reset the valuation already embeds more cycle risk, so the stock is hard to fight near term. The same logic is applied to most hardware: as long as pricing holds, earnings grow into the multiples.

Rates: the back end of the Treasury curve is still bidless. PCE came in lighter but barely changed the long-end trajectory. A October Fed move looks less likely after softer inflation and Fed speak, and hikes have been taken out of the front end, but the stress remains further out the curve. Forward inflation expectations are inching higher alongside the S&P 500 and heating oil.
Payrolls and ISM are the next catalysts. After strong PMIs, ISM has upside asymmetry for bonds: if it merely fails to confirm another acceleration, duration could get some relief.

France: the 2027 budget is due today. Prime Minister Lecornu targets about €54bn of adjustment to bring the deficit to 5.0% in 2027 from 5.4% in 2026, versus about 6.5% without new measures. The OAT/Bund spread is about 120bp. The government has no majority and this is the last budget before the presidential election, so the opposition response matters more than the document. Even a 5% deficit leaves debt rising.

The desk sees higher French yields worsening the debt arithmetic and building political support for restraint. It flags a weaker EUR as a more interesting tail than OATs, if a future domestically focused government confronts Brussels over France's EU contribution. France is not Greece, Portugal or Spain, so externally imposed austerity is much less plausible.

French equities: heavy client selling of French domestics is rational because taxation is likely part of the fiscal solution, especially for regulated and utility-like businesses. With spreads near 120bp and positioning heavily skewed, the desk thinks it would not take much good news to squeeze. Le Pen's alternative budget is expected in the coming weeks, likely before parliamentary debates start on October 13.

Iran/oil: little new. The Iranian delegation left New York and the sides remain far apart, though talks continue through Qatar. The desk wants a deal so the rest of the equity market can join the rally.

Risk: Nasdaq is near its highs and the desk thinks the market is still underexposed. Micro is bullish against an ugly macro backdrop. Credit and rates make broad beta difficult, but gross exposure is working. Europe and the Russell are lagging and vol hedges are relatively cheap. With stable rates, AI can keep lifting the index. If productivity growth resembles the late 1990s, equities can tolerate higher real rates, though not uniformly (bad for small caps, lower-quality balance sheets and the consumer).

risk_factors: Long-end rates: the back end of the curve is bidless, and a rise in yields would pressure broad beta, small caps, lower-quality balance sheets and the consumer.
Hardware cycle: concern about where the memory and hardware cycle peaks, though the desk says valuations already embed more cycle risk.
Data center moratoriums: Polymarket prices 20-30% odds of state-level moratoriums by end 2027, and power shortages compound the compute shortage.
French fiscal and political risk: no parliamentary majority, debt still rising at a 5% deficit, and a possible confrontation with Brussels that could weaken the EUR.
Iran talks stalling into the US midterms, which holds back the rest of the equity market.
Macro backdrop described as genuinely ugly, with credit and rates making broad beta difficult.
vol_and_positioning: Vol hedges remain relatively cheap while Nasdaq threatens its highs.
The desk thinks the market still feels underexposed despite being near highs.
Positioning in French domestics is heavily skewed after heavy client selling, which raises squeeze risk on any good news.
Forward inflation expectations are inching higher alongside the S&P 500 and heating oil.
The chart attached to the note is titled implied vol on a 3-month 25-delta put on the long bond versus the 2-year (Bloomberg, as of 1 Oct 2026), with no figures given in the text.
geopolitical: Iran/oil: the Iranian delegation has left New York and the sides remain far apart, though talks are alive through Qatar. The desk asks who moves first and whether either side wants this to roll toward the midterms.

France: the 2027 budget is presented with no government majority. The opposition response and Le Pen's alternative budget, expected before parliamentary debates start October 13, are the key variables. A possible future confrontation with Brussels over France's EU contribution is flagged as a tail risk.

tension_points.bear_case: Investors worry about where the cycle peaks and at some point ASPs rise too quickly and profits become too large to last. The desk says valuation already embeds more cycle risk after the multiple reset.
